Full-year 2026 CapEx is guided to approximately $220 billion, heavily front-loaded into custom Trainium2 silicon clusters and liquid-cooled AI data center capacity.

Row 4: Operational Execution Audit & Earnings Call Forensic Q&A Highlights
ANALYST AUDIT
What Management Did Right (Operational Tailwinds)
1. AWS Re-Acceleration (+39.3% YoY): AWS surged to $42.23B with 39.36% operating margins, delivering its fastest top-line growth in nearly five years on massive enterprise Bedrock adoption.
2. All-Time Record Operating Margin (13.90%): Worldwide consolidated EBIT reached $28.08B (+61.1% YoY), proving that regional fulfillment automation and advertising mix are driving structural operating leverage.
3. High-Margin Digital Advertising Engine: Advertising grew +19.5% YoY to $19.81B, scaling through Prime Video ad tiers and sponsored product auctions heading into high-teens Q4 growth.
4. International Segment Profitability: International operations generated $1,717M in EBIT (4.2% margin), cementing permanent profitability across major European and Asian marketplaces.
Execution Headwinds & Capital Allocation Pressures
1. FY2026 CapEx Escalation to ~$220B: Raising annual cash capital spending to $220B represents a major cash burn hurdle that will depress free cash flow conversion well into 2027.
2. Negative Quarterly True FCF (-$54.90B): CapEx and SBC combined to burn -$54.9B of economic cash flow in Q3, eliminating expectations for near-term share repurchase authorizations.
3. Optical Advertising Pacing Shift: Advertising decelerated from +19.5% in Q2 due to the calendar shift of Prime Day, requiring management to defend the underlying growth trajectory.
4. GAAP EPS Miss ($1.89 vs $1.96): Increased data center infrastructure depreciation and energy costs trimmed headline net income to $20.69B (-2.4% YoY).

Brian Nowak (Morgan Stanley) • Topic: $220B FY26 CapEx, Negative Quarterly FCF (-$34.8B) & ROIC Underwriting

Analyst Question: "Andy and Brian, Q3 CapEx accelerated to $77.26 billion, pushing quarterly reported free cash flow to -$34.84 billion, and you guided full-year 2026 CapEx to $220 billion. How should institutional investors underwrite the durability of AWS margins and return on capital on this level of spending?"

Executive Response: "CEO Andy Jassy explained that AWS net sales grew 39.3% YoY to a $184 billion annualized run rate with 39.4% operating margins, generating $16.62 billion in segment EBIT in a single quarter. The overwhelming majority of the $220 billion CapEx is for contracted generative AI infrastructure and custom Trainium2 chips where demand dramatically outstrips available capacity, giving Amazon high conviction in rapid multi-year payback."

Doug Anmuth (JPMorgan) • Topic: AWS Deceleration Concerns vs 39.3% Growth & Trainium2 Chip Supply

Analyst Question: "Andy, AWS delivered an extraordinary 39.3% growth rate to $42.23 billion. Could you unpack the contribution between core enterprise cloud migrations versus generative AI workloads on Bedrock, and what are the primary supply chain gating factors for Trainium2 silicon?"

Executive Response: "Andy Jassy noted that AWS growth was powered by both large-scale migrations of traditional workloads and massive enterprise adoption of Bedrock and Trainium2. Trainium2 clusters are virtually 100% committed upon delivery, offering clients 40% to 50% better price-performance than commercial GPUs, which is driving accelerated customer retention."

Ross Sandler (Barclays) • Topic: Advertising Growth (+12% vs +19.5% Prior) & Prime Day Timing Impact

Analyst Question: "Brian, advertising revenue grew 12% YoY in Q3 after growing 19.5% in Q2, while you guide advertising back to the high teens in Q4. Can you clarify how much of the Q3 deceleration was purely Prime Day timing versus macro ad demand?"

Executive Response: "CFO Brian Olsavsky confirmed that Prime Day shifted entirely to Q2 in 2026 for most major geographies, whereas in 2025 it occurred in Q3. Excluding this 400 bps shift and foreign exchange headwinds, baseline advertising demand remains exceptionally healthy, leading to strong visibility for high-teens ad growth during the Q4 holiday quarter."
